formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD a) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b)) → (∠ a:b:c = ∠ c:b:d)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD a) (h2 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) : ∠ a:b:c = ∠ c:b:d := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD a) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD c) ∧ (twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD d)) → (∠ a:b:c = ∠ d:b:a ∧ ∠ c:b:a = ∠ d:b:c)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD a) (h2 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD b) (h3 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD c) (h4 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD d) : ∠ a:b:c = ∠ d:b:a ∧ ∠ c:b:a = ∠ d:b:c := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (A : Point) (B : Point) (C : Point) (D : Point) (E : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD E)) → (∠ A:E:C = ∠ D:E:B ∧ ∠ C:E:B = ∠ A:E:D)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (A B C D E : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD E) : ∠ A:E:C = ∠ D:E:B ∧ ∠ C:E:B = ∠ A:E:D := by

formalizations.formalization: ∀ (a : Point) (b : Point) (c : Point) (d : Point) (e : Point) (AB : Line) (CD : Line), ((twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD e) ∧ (distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) ∧ (distinctPointsOnLine c d CD)) → (∠ a:e:c = ∠ d:e:b ∧ ∠ c:e:b = ∠ a:e:d)
formalizations.full_output: theorem example_thm (a b c d e : Point) (AB CD : Line) (h1 : twoLinesIntersectAtPoint AB CD e) (h2 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) (h3 : distinctPointsOnLine c d CD) : ∠ a:e:c = ∠ d:e:b ∧ ∠ c:e:b = ∠ a:e:d := by

reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c d e : Point) (AB CD : Line), distinctPointsOnLine a b AB ∧ distinctPointsOnLine c d CD ∧ e.onLine AB ∧ e.onLine CD ∧ CD ≠ AB ∧ (between d e c) ∧ (between a e b) → (∠ a:e:c = ∠ d:e:b) ∧ (∠ c:e:b = ∠ a:e:d)
nl_statement: If two straight-lines cut one another then they make the vertically opposite angles equal to one another.For let the two straight-lines $AB$ and $CD$ cut one another at the point $E$. I say that  angle $AEC$ is equal to (angle) $DEB$, and (angle) $CEB$ to (angle) $AED$. <prf>  Thus, the remainder $CEA$ is equal to the remainder $BED$ [C.N.~3]. Similarly, it can be shown that $CEB$ and $DEA$ are also equal.Thus, if two straight-lines cut one another then they make the vertically opposite angles equal to one another.
